title: Natural tensor comparison at an algebra prime and its contracted base prime
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, and put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Localizations and spectra are [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For an $A$-module $P$ and an $R$-module $N$, give $P_{\mathfrak q}$ its $R_{\mathfrak p}$-action through the canonical ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$, $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$. There are canonical $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear isomorphisms
$$\alpha_{P,N}:(P\otimes_R N)_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_R N,\qquad (x\otimes n)/s\longmapsto(x/s)\otimes n,$$
$$\beta_{P,N}:P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_R N\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}N_{\mathfrak p},\qquad z\otimes n\longmapsto z\otimes(n/1).$$
Write $c_{P,N}=\beta_{P,N}\alpha_{P,N}$. For every $A$-linear map $v:P\to P'$, these isomorphisms satisfy
$$c_{P',N}\circ(v\otimes_R1_N)_{\mathfrak q}=(v_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}1_{N_{\mathfrak p}})\circ c_{P,N}.$$
If $N$ already has an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module structure restricting to its given $R$-action, then $N\to N_{\mathfrak p}$, $n\mapsto n/1$, is an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear isomorphism with inverse $n/t\mapsto t^{-1}n$; composing $c_{P,N}$ with this inverse on the second tensor factor identifies $(v\otimes_R1_N)_{\mathfrak q}$ with $v_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}1_N$.

proof.text: Put $T=A\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$. The inverse image $\mathfrak p$ is prime: $1\notin\mathfrak p$, and $ab\in\mathfrak p$ implies $\varphi(a)\varphi(b)\in\mathfrak q$, hence $a\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$. Thus $S,T$ are multiplicative and $\varphi(S)\subset T$. The fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], applied to the rings themselves, makes $r/t\mapsto\varphi(r)/\varphi(t)$ well defined: an equality witnessed by $u\in S$ maps to an equality witnessed by $\varphi(u)\in T$. The sum and product formulas show that this is a unital ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$; restriction of the $A_{\mathfrak q}$-action gives the asserted $R_{\mathfrak p}$-action on $P_{\mathfrak q}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] to $R\to A$, $T$, $M=P$, and $N$. It gives the $A$-linear isomorphism $\alpha_{P,N}$ with the required formula. It is $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear as well: an $A$-linear map between $A_{\mathfrak q}$-modules commutes with multiplication by $s\in T$ and therefore with its inverse (apply the map to $s(s^{-1}w)=w$). It consequently commutes with every scalar $a/s$.

proof.text: Use the localization criterion stated in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product]. The identity $P_{\mathfrak q}\to P_{\mathfrak q}$ is a localization at $S$: every $t\in S$ acts invertibly via $\varphi(t)/1$, every element is already an identity image with denominator $1$, and equality of identity images is witnessed by $1\in S$. The map $N\to N_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization at $S$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Apply the cited tensor theorem with its ring $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, its first pair $M=M'=P_{\mathfrak q}$, and its second pair $N,N'=N_{\mathfrak p}$. It says that the $R$-linear map $\beta:z\otimes n\mapsto z\otimes(n/1)$ is a localization at $S$.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, proof, displayed tensor identities and N_p = N; expanded using Tags 00DK and 00DL

proof.text: Write $X=P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_RN$ and $Y=P_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}N_{\mathfrak p}$. For $t\in S$, multiplication by $t$ on $X$ has inverse $z\otimes n\mapsto(t^{-1}z)\otimes n$; this map exists by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], since multiplication by $t^{-1}$ on $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is $R$-linear. The localization criterion [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] now makes $\beta$ bijective. Indeed, if $\beta(x)=\beta(x')$, some $t\in S$ kills $x-x'$, so $x=x'$. Every $y\in Y$ is $t^{-1}\beta(x)=\beta(t^{-1}x)$, so it is in the image. Finally, the formula $\beta(az\otimes n)=az\otimes(n/1)=a\beta(z\otimes n)$ for $a\in A_{\mathfrak q}$ proves $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linearity on generators, hence everywhere. This is the required isomorphism $\beta_{P,N}$.

proof.text: For an $A$-linear $v:P\to P'$, both sides of the claimed naturality identity send $(x\otimes n)/s$ to $(v(x)/s)\otimes(n/1)$, using the formulas for $\alpha,\beta$ and localized maps [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. These pure fractions generate: write any tensor numerator as a finite sum of pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and divide the sum by its common denominator $s$. Equality on these generators proves the identity for $c_{P,N}=\beta_{P,N}\alpha_{P,N}$.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, proof, displayed tensor identities and N_p = N; expanded using Tags 00DK and 00DL

proof.text: If $N$ is already an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module with the prescribed restriction, put $\delta(n/t)=t^{-1}n$. This is well defined by the fraction relation [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]: $u(t'n-tn')=0$ implies $t'n=tn'$ since $u$ acts invertibly, and then $t^{-1}n=(t')^{-1}n'$. The fraction addition and scalar formulas make $\delta$ $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear. The unit $\eta(n)=n/1$ is also $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear because it commutes with $R$ and with inverses of multiplication by $t\in S$. We have $\delta\eta(n)=n$ and $\eta\delta(n/t)=n/t$, the latter after multiplying by the invertible $t$. Compose $c$ with $1\otimes\delta$. Both composites with the maps induced by $v$ send $(x\otimes n)/s$ to $(v(x)/s)\otimes n$, proving the final identification on the generators from Step 5.
